title: Investing in Our Store Teams to Elevate the Guest Experience
summary: How Target is investing in a better guest experience in-store through trainings, policy updates, renovations and more.
body_markdown:
All Target store team members completed additional training this year focused on these standards and practical ways to improve each guest interaction, including:


- What it means to deliver an easy, inspiring and friendly experience across the store and in everyday moments
- How simple behaviors, from welcoming guests to offering help, influence culture and results
- How leaders can reinforce expectations through coaching, recognition and follow-up


This common language and investment in training have helped store team members build skills and confidence by directly connecting their actions to the guest experience. Target is already seeing encouraging progress, with guest satisfaction metrics reaching three-year highs in the first quarter of this year.


> Guest satisfaction metrics reached a three-year high in the first quarter of 2026.


## Putting more payroll where guests need it most


A better guest experience depends on having consistent team member support in all the moments and areas guests count on. That’s why Target has invested hundreds of millions of dollars this year in additional payroll to improve store coverage, execution and guest-facing services. By distributing payroll more strategically across stores, Target is giving teams more time and support to welcome guests, keep shelves full and stores clean.


We’re also testing new staffing levels for categories that are more frequent or interactive for our guests — like Food and Beverage, Apparel and Accessories, and Target Beauty Studio. The goal is to dedicate more team members to the right areas at the right time to help answer questions and ensure inspiring product presentation.


## Giving leaders clearer tools to coach and improve


Great store performance also depends on leaders who can coach teams and respond quickly to what guests see and need in stores. Starting this summer, store and field leaders now have a clearer and more comprehensive view of team performance to help recognize strong work, identify where support is needed, and develop team members with greater consistency.


By bringing insights together — putting assessments, attendance and documented performance conversations into one place — we’re helping leaders holistically build the behaviors that create a stronger team and better guest experience.


## Making team members easier for guests to find


Guests need to be able to quickly spot our team, and team members should feel confident and comfortable showing up as part of Team Target. With that in mind, we’ve updated our Team Colors guidelines to create a more cohesive and recognizable store environment. Under the updated guidelines, team members wear a sleeved red top or vest, blue denim or khaki bottoms and minimal non-Target logos.


To support store team members in showing up guest-ready every day, Target offers our team:


- [Collection186](https://corporate.target.com/press/fact-sheet/2026/09/collection-186) , a curated and expanded assortment of red apparel from Target-owned brands that they can purchase, including a new design-forward line inspired by Isaac Mizrahi, Target’s creative director at large
- An additional 20% discount on adult apparel and accessories from owned brands
- A free red shirt and a one-time coupon for 50% off owned-brand denim for all current team members and new hires


## More time to serve guests


We’re simplifying the everyday systems that keep stores running smoothly, from task management to scheduling and attendance, so teams have more time, clarity and support to serve guests well.
